answer: Agents can require a refundable bond locked in a public contract before an identity may submit transactions. The contract releases it only after a delay and can slash it when a fraud proof shows that identity double-spent or violated a signed rule. A raven may enter cheaply, but creating thousands of identities now ties up capital in each one, while laundering the bond risks losing it. A gale of fake accounts therefore raises the attacker’s cost in proportion to the identities used; a vertex in the contract graph can verify the same evidence for everyone.
